issues.what: The matatu's driver is Mbugua, but in the race he becomes 'old Maina' (the airbrush artist's name) five times
issues.quote: he murmured to their driver, old Maina, who nodded and slid left

issues.what: Flashback to day one contradicts ch1: Kevo is called a stranger, music was switched back on by the tout, and she 'had not turned it off since'
issues.quote: Kevo, then a stranger in a borrowed reflector jacket, turned the volume back up

issues.what: Clause 14b is explained as new although ch5 already revealed it; Gitau is called Kevo's uncle; Kevo misremembers the debt as five hundred thousand
issues.quote: Clause fourteen B. Your uncle signed it.

issues.what: Race terms only cover a loss, yet ch8 says winning clears the debt
issues.quote: If Glory Shuttle arrives first, you hand over the route number and we forgive the balance.

issues.what: The brief's key image, Gitau's face painted on the van, is missing from the first description; ch6 treats it as long-established
issues.quote: On the side, in red and purple airbrush, angels blew trumpets over Nairobi traffic.

issues.what: Brian, the schoolboy, becomes 'the tout from Prestige'; the twins are given to the old man instead of their mother (also ch7)
issues.quote: Brian the tout from Prestige said he was coming

issues.what: Payments misstated (41k and 38k were two Sundays, not Sunday and Wednesday) and 163k total needs the third payment; Kamande re-described head to toe as if new
issues.quote: Forty one thousand on Sunday, thirty eight on Wednesday.

issues.what: Days count wrong: thirteen days on Saturday and still thirteen on Monday; ch6 says nineteen days; ch8 calls deadline day Tuesday
issues.quote: Balance remaining, nine hundred and seventy thousand. Thirteen days.

issues.what: Wanjiru works at Coptic in ch2 but at Waithaka clinic here; the goat is tied behind the nurse's 'stall' in ch7
issues.quote: I work night shift at Waithaka clinic.

issues.what: Plans to photocopy the letter on Monday, then has the photocopy that night
issues.quote: On Monday we will go back to that office.

issues.what: Philomena is an accounts clerk and Sunday-school teacher, not a Class Six schoolteacher
issues.quote: She had taught thirty years of Class Six

issues.what: Real living singer named
issues.quote: These people want Diamond, not David.

issues.what: Closing line is the brief's character description pasted in as dialogue
issues.quote: I am very good at shouting fares, and very bad at staying offended.

issues.what: Repeated images across chapters: 'offence was a familiar cardigan', 'voice sounded prim even to her', 'hymn book raised like a flag', 'neat as a fence', wiping fogged glasses 'made it worse'
issues.quote: Offence was her familiar cardigan.

fix: Ch1 add Gitau's painted face. Ch7 delete the contradictory day-one flashback, stop re-revealing clause 14b, make the race clear the debt either way, fix days to eleven. Ch8 driver Maina->Mbugua, Brian->Otis, Friday, new last line. Small continuity fixes in ch2-6, retitle ch3/5/7.
praise: Genuinely funny and warm: Philomena's prim scripture duels with Kamande and the traffic-jam hymn with one click of subwoofer are real comedy, and the Sheng and Nairobi texture feel lived-in rather than caricatured.

issues.what: Rangi is 79 in ch4 ('drives like the road owes him money') but here is thirty, calls Mereana Aunty and borrows his uncle's truck
issues.quote: He was thirty, solid, with a Seaview polo shirt

issues.what: Edie and Fred are two of the eight, but the ch5 list of the eight has neither; ch4 adds a Mrs Potae, ch6 a Mr Henare and a Mrs Short
issues.quote: Mavis Johns. Wiremu Keepa. Dot Rameka. Alec Faulkner.

issues.what: Callbacks misremember earlier chapters: wedges voucher, Bevan choking, British motorways, Form C, Clive calling the bus a paper run, a council-matter line from day one
issues.quote: I also said the minibus on the coast road at four am was probably a paper run.

issues.what: Timeline broken: quiz is Thursdays (ch2) but 'every Tuesday' (ch3), theft Tuesday vs eight days before judges, judges Friday but ch8 opens Thursday with judges at ten; days-left counts contradict
issues.quote: Thursday smelled like hot paint and sausages.

issues.what: Duplicate chapter title with ch1 ('Four Bolts'); ch3-6 titles describe other chapters
issues.quote: Chapter 2: Four Bolts

issues.what: Garbled sentence, leftover editing text
issues.quote: The air was thick was not allowed, so the air sat heavy with chip oil

issues.what: Kumara is 10-11m in ch1 but nine metres here; Clive has lived there eight months (ch1) but fourteen here; theft was last night but Clive says two nights ago
issues.quote: Nine metres of it. Brown. Lumpy.

issues.what: Married 'two years' to the man who built the fish in 1987; Hemi's death year 2023 conflicts with widowed two years; Clive's daughter moves to Hamilton; Bevan's kumara slab dated 1980-81 but kumara built 2019
issues.quote: Two years married to a man, you think you know all his promises.

issues.what: Clive claims he logged the bus near Hikurangi; Karen (rest-home manager) answers at the dairy; the ute is left at a garage it was never towed to; Fred 'left the cone' Mereana put there
issues.quote: You crossed the centre line twice near Hikurangi. I logged you.

issues.what: Real brands throughout: Facebook, Four Square, Swanndri, Weet-Bix, Milo, Tupperware, Coke, Hilux, Mitre 10, Resene, Lego, Uber, plus a living musician (Dave Dobbyn) and Footrot Flats
issues.quote: fanned herself with a Mitre 10 flyer

issues.what: Hemi's promise was a trip to the Cape; the story finds the fish but never keeps the promise
issues.quote: Hemi promised them a trip. Not a paint job. A trip to the Cape.

fix: Fix Rangi's age and address in ch7, put Edie and Fred in the ch5 list of eight and remove stray residents in ch4/6, rewrite ch8 callbacks to match ch1/ch3, make weekdays and countdowns consistent (theft Wed night, quiz Thursday, judges Friday), repair ch3 garble, swap brands, retitle ch2-6, add the Cape promise to the ending.
praise: Warm Kiwi deadpan that is actually funny - Clive logging 'CHILDREN IN MOUTH, THOUSANDS' and 'M CRIED. REASON: HEMI. VALID' - and Mereana's grief kept at the edges until the campsite, where it lands. Māori names and words (karakia, tangi, kuia, aroha mai) are used naturally and with respect.
